data.title: Adapalene gel (0.1%, 0.3%)
data.summary: VII Anti-acne — Retinoids · Third-generation (polyaromatic) topical retinoid — naphthoic acid derivative
data.body:
_Topicals · VII Anti-acne — Retinoids_

**Class:** Third-generation (polyaromatic) topical retinoid — naphthoic acid derivative

## Mechanism of action
- Selective for RAR-β and RAR-γ → comedolytic, normalises keratinisation
- Strong anti-inflammatory action (inhibits neutrophil lipoxygenase, AP-1, TLR-2)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acne vulgaris — first-line (0.1% gel, available OTC in the USA; 0.3% for more severe)
- Fixed combinations: adapalene 0.1%/0.3% + BPO 2.5%; adapalene + clindamycin
- Maintenance after oral therapy or isotretinoin; PIH, keratosis pilaris, Darier disease (off-label)

## Dose & formulations
- Pea-sized amount once daily at night (can be applied in the morning — chemically stable)

## Adverse effects
- Dryness, redness, stinging — less irritating than tretinoin or tazarotene
- Photosensitivity (mild)

## Contraindications
- Eczema, sunburn; pregnancy (precaution)

## Drug interactions
- Stable with BPO and in light — can be combined in one product

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid in pregnancy (precaution).

## Viva points
- Most tolerable topical retinoid
- Light-stable and BPO-stable — combined in one gel
- RAR-β/γ selective

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.46; Khopkar ch.24. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
